title: The folds and cusps of the perturbed complex square
statement: For the real smooth map \(F_\varepsilon:\mathbb C\to\mathbb C\), \(F_\varepsilon(z)=z^2+\varepsilon\bar z\), \(\varepsilon>0\), determine the critical set, critical values, local singularity types, and the regular-fibre cardinalities.
status: As of 9 November 2026: settled. The critical circle is \(|z|=\varepsilon/2\); its image is the three-cusped curve \(\varepsilon^2(e^{2it}/4+e^{-it}/2)\), with cusps where \(e^{3it}=1\) and folds elsewhere. There are four preimages in its interior and two in its exterior. The explicit treatment is \citet[\S1, Example 6, pp.~4--5]{arnold1968singularities}, published in 1968 from 1966 lectures. This repeats the earlier indexed question; it does not create a new problem. See \citep{arnold1968singularities}.

title: Algebraic classification of Anosov diffeomorphisms
statement: Is every Anosov diffeomorphism of a closed manifold topologically conjugate to an affine Anosov map of an infranilmanifold?
status: As of November 2026, unresolved in general in the checked literature; see Spatzier’s Conjecture 2.3. The weaker manifold-realization question also remains open. The smooth-category replacement is too strong. See \citep{smale1967dynamical,spatzier2016rigidity,deremainkar2023anosov,farrellgogolev2012exotic}.

title: Structural stability of Morse--Smale systems
statement: Are Morse--Smale maps and flows \(C^1\) structurally stable?
status: Affirmatively solved; 1968 circulation, 1969 Russian and 1970 English publication. See \citep{palissmale1970stability}.

title: Necessity of Morse--Smale conditions
statement: Must structural stability imply the Morse--Smale conditions?
status: No; hyperbolic toral automorphisms and their suspension flows provide counterexamples. See \citep{smale1967dynamical}.

title: Density of Morse--Smale systems
statement: Are Morse--Smale systems dense on every closed manifold?
status: No in general; an open family of Anosov systems supplies an obstruction. See \citep{smale1967dynamical}.

title: Density of structurally stable fields
statement: Are structurally stable vector fields dense on every compact manifold?
status: No in general, by Smale’s 1966 counterexample, already published at the time of the question. See \citep{smale1966nondensity}.

title: Density of Axiom A
statement: Are Axiom A diffeomorphisms \(C^1\)-dense on every closed manifold?
status: No in general; Abraham--Smale, 1970. See \citep{abrahamsmale1970nongenericity}.

title: Periodic density from hyperbolic nonwandering set
statement: Does hyperbolicity of \(\Omega(f)\) force \(\Omega(f)=\overline{\operatorname{Per}(f)}\)?
status: No in general; Kurata, 1979. See \citep{kurata1979hyperbolic}.

title: Uniqueness of the vanishing identity-viscosity limit
statement: Under what hypotheses do the solutions of \(u_t+A(u)u_x=\epsilon u_{xx}\) have a unique limit as \(\epsilon\downarrow0\)?
status: As of November 2026: Bianchini--Bressan solve the smooth strictly hyperbolic small-total-variation case. The notes do not determine a universal large-data conjecture. See \citep{bianchinibressan2005viscosity}.

title: Representative pair observables: moment hypotheses and concentration
statement: A precise question extracted from the representativeness argument is which moment and mixing hypotheses justify concentration of \(N^{-1}\sum_{i\ne j}f(x_i-x_j)\), and whether an arbitrary real even \(L^1\) kernel permits the claimed finite linear variance. Minlos’s later Problem 3 asks for quantitative inequalities in this argument. This entry does not index an unspecified all-density existence conjecture.
status: As of November 2026: the finite-variance claim under bare \(L^1\) is false even for an ideal gas. The chapter supplies a complete conditional correction with an explicit four-point bound, an \(L^1\) truncation conclusion, and counterexamples. These are checked critical annotations, not a claim that a previously open C/D problem has been solved. Establishing the assumed correlation bound in an interacting model remains model- and regime-dependent. See \citep{minlos1968lectures,pulvirentitsagkarogiannis2015finite,kunatsagkarogiannis2018density}.

title: Realizability of a full correlation hierarchy
statement: Characterize the symmetric locally finite factorial moment measures of probability laws on locally finite configurations, distinguishing existence from uniqueness.
status: As of 9 November 2026: Lenard's symmetry, positivity and normalization characterization supplies existence; determinacy requires additional conditions. See \citep{lenard1975characterization,lenard1973correlation}.

title: Helgason spherical support problem on a smooth Hadamard manifold
statement: For complete simply connected negatively curved smooth \(M\), do zero integrals of \(f\in C_c^\infty(M)\) over all geodesic spheres enclosing a closed ball \(B\) imply \(\operatorname{supp}f\subset B\)?
status: As of 9 November 2026: verified for real-analytic metrics; a general smooth-metric resolution was not found. The precise source is Quinto's Problem 4.1, not a ray-transform support theorem. See \citep{quinto2008helgason}.

title: Entire convex Monge--Ampere rigidity
statement: Must every convex entire solution of \(\det D^2u=1\) be quadratic?
status: As of 9 November 2026: yes in all dimensions, by the J\"orgens--Calabi--Pogorelov theorem; convex viscosity solutions are included. See \citep{caffarellili2003extension}.

title: Entire minimal-graph Bernstein problem
statement: For which \(n\) is every smooth entire minimal graph over \(\mathbb R^n\) an affine hyperplane?
status: As of 9 November 2026: exactly \(n\le7\); nonaffine entire minimal graphs exist for \(n\ge8\). See \citep{bombieridegiorgigiusti1969minimal}.

title: Metric rigidity of a Sobolev composition isometry
statement: If a smooth diffeomorphism of closed Riemannian manifolds induces an isometry of their full \(H^1\) inner products by pullback, must it preserve their metrics?
status: As of 9 November 2026: yes, by volume and Dirichlet-form recovery; the composition condition is essential. See \citep{arendt2017diffusion}.

title: Escape of geodesics on a complete noncompact positive-Ricci three-manifold
statement: On a complete connected noncompact Riemannian three-manifold with positive Ricci curvature, does every geodesic go to infinity?
status: As of 13 November 2026: not checked against the literature after the revised reading of P000172; the earlier volume reading (answered yes by Yau's theorem, \citep{yau1976function}) no longer applies.

title: Diffeomorphism type of equal-period closed-geodesic manifolds
statement: Must a closed simply connected Riemannian manifold whose prime unit-speed geodesics all have the same period be diffeomorphic to a compact rank-one symmetric space?
status: As of 9 November 2026: cohomology is constrained to the rank-one symmetric models; the unrestricted smooth classification was not found resolved. The result of \citet[definition on p.~1 and Main Theorem on p.~3]{lisong2026zoll} assumes simple closed prime geodesics of a common period, as well as an entire Grauert tube, and proves metric rigidity only for the complex-projective cohomology type. Those additional hypotheses do not remove the gap for the notebook's question. See \citep{lisong2026zoll}.

title: Existence of contact structures in dimension three
statement: Which closed smooth three-manifolds admit a contact plane field?
status: As of 9 November 2026: exactly the orientable ones: necessity follows from the contact volume orientation and sufficiency from Martinet's theorem. See \citep{martinet1971contact,eliashberg1992contact}.

title: Invariant distributions for the Lorentz form
statement: For \(SO_0(2,1)\)-invariant \(T\in\mathcal D'(\mathbb R^3)\) and nonzero \(P\in\mathbb C[t]\), does \(P(\partial_x^2+\partial_y^2-\partial_z^2)T=0\) force \(T\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}\)?
status: Solved before this occurrence: the affirmative answer is the rank-one case of \citet[Theorem~1]{harishchandra1965algebra}. Checked as of 9 November 2026. No identical precise question was located in the supplied earlier index. See \citep{harishchandra1965algebra}.

title: Geometric orbit quotients for affine reductive actions
statement: For an affine variety over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero with a reductive group action, when does the invariant-theoretic categorical quotient have individual orbits as its fibers?
status: Solved before the March 1967 report: exactly when all orbits are closed. The modern verification is \citet[Theorem~2.2.1 and Definition~2.1.4]{berczi2016quotients}, in the framework of \citet{mumford1965invariant}. The broader notebook question is recorded with its quotient-category ambiguity. Status checked 9 November 2026.

title: Global boundary completion with trivial auxiliary bundles
statement: For the admissible continuous normal Fredholm family of an elliptic convolution system over \(S^*\Gamma\), when can finitely many globally defined potential terms and boundary equations, with trivial auxiliary bundles, produce an invertible completed normal family?
status: Solved in 1967 under the Vishik--Eskin regularity and noncritical-order hypotheses: the family index must be the class of a signed trivial bundle, and this condition is sufficient with \(E=0\); see \citet[\S3, Theorems~1.3 and 2.3]{vishikeskin1967normally}. Received 27 April 1967; earlier circulation beyond the present seminar evidence was not established. Status checked 9 November 2026. The overwritten connective in the notebook remains uncertain. See \citep{vishikeskin1967normally}.
